Figure 10 shows an example of a heating day misclassified as a cooling day for a single model. The day was misclassified as a heating day, and preheating was performed from 14:00 to 18:00, resulting in a large reduction in cooling load later in the day because the preheating increased both the heating and the cooling set points2; however, once the peak period begins at 18:00, the increased cooling set point is reset to normal, resulting in increased cooling energy consumption. Essentially, we tried to preheat when precooling would have been appropriate, resulting in increased load during the peak. The solution was to avoid preheating or precooling when the average daily outdoor temperature is near the threshold (66°F) because it is hard to predict whether precooling or preheating would be the more appropriate action.
